title: Sensex jumps 1,502 points, recovering Monday's fall, as oil eases and foreign money returns
dek: The Nifty closed at 25,819, up 1.85%, led by consumer-goods makers and private banks. Steel and telecom shares lagged.
body:
India's main stock indices posted their biggest one-day gain in weeks on Wednesday, almost wiping out Monday's slide, as crude oil prices eased, the rupee firmed and foreign investors kept buying. The BSE Sensex closed at 83,938.28, up 1,502.29 points or 1.82%, and the NSE Nifty 50 ended at 25,819.25, up 469.60 points or 1.85%.

The rally came two days after the Sensex shed 1,484 points on Monday, when banks and metal shares slid. Wednesday's gains were led by large companies; smaller stocks were weaker, a sign that the recovery was not broad-based, analysts said.

## What moved

Consumer-goods makers led the market. The Nifty FMCG index rose 3.8%, the biggest gain among sectors, with Hindustan Unilever the top gainer on both exchanges and Nestle India and ITC also among the leaders. Private banks, pharmaceutical companies and financial services followed, with ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and HDFC Life rising. IndiGo, Trent, Eternal, Infosys and Bharat Electronics were also among the gainers, and Reliance Industries added to the index's rise, reports said.

Metal, media, chemicals, real estate and telecom stocks ended lower. Tata Steel, ONGC, JSW Steel, Hindalco and Bharti Airtel were among the main losers. Tata Steel has been under pressure since it agreed on Sunday to sell its tubes and coated-steel businesses to APL Apollo for up to ₹28,000 crore.

## Why markets rose

Three things helped, according to market reports. Brent crude, India's benchmark for imported oil, eased to around $91 a barrel during Indian trading hours, lowering worries about the import bill and inflation. Oil has been volatile because of the US naval blockade of Iran and Iran's tightening of the Strait of Hormuz, and because of Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian refineries, which hit two more plants overnight.

Foreign portfolio investors have also returned. One analyst said foreign investors had put more than $14 billion into Indian shares so far in November. The rupee traded between about 92.30 and 92.42 to the US dollar, its strongest in seven months, reports said.

Economic data has added to the mood. An index of business activity published by the rating agency ICRA on Wednesday showed activity grew 12.8% from a year earlier in October, the fastest in three years.

## What analysts said

Shrikant Chouhan, head of equity research at Kotak Neo, said 26,000 was "the immediate trigger" for the Nifty and that, if it held above that level, the index could retest its record zone near 26,300; in the very short term he expected it to trade between 25,000 and 26,300. Ajit Mishra of Religare Broking said the rebound showed that buying interest remained intact, and expected banking stocks to pause after their recent run, reports said.

## What to watch

Investors are waiting for the findings of the United States' "excess capacity" trade investigation into India and 15 other economies, which reports say could bring new US tariffs as soon as this week. The Reserve Bank of India's next monetary policy decision is due in early December, and economists at SBI expect any rate rise then to be limited to 25 basis points, reports said. Oil prices, and any news on talks between Washington and Tehran, remain the biggest swing factor for Indian markets.

Closing figures are from the exchanges as reported; sector and stock moves are as reported at the close.
